batch_1.Q1_length: 14 chapters, ~50k words: room for side characters to get their own turns, a dungeon delve for cores, a second deal that goes wrong, a longer climb to the ending
batch_1.Q2_gates: Write it all through: every chapter written and checked without stopping; gates become review points Isaac goes through at the end (approve, note or re-brief any chapter); the whole novella delivered as one Markdown file
batch_1.Q3_age: Twenty at the open: an adult from page one
batch_1.Q4_dream: A debt to a warrior: a fighter saved him once and would take no payment; a merchant cannot stand an unpaid account, so he means to become what she was

batch_2.Q5_start: The Hundred Crowns (the Midmarch): petty kings along both roads, a toll every mile, war supply sold to both sides, comic names; nearly every crown owes Nalūn, so the road up leads to the salt cities in later books
batch_2.Q6_power: Provenance: everything remembers who held it. Body Path walked with Anamnesis (Medium lens, faded violet): a blade he handles gives back its past owners' blows for his shoulders to repeat; he learns to fight from the dead men's swords he buys and sells. Cost: every past he reads stays in him. Counter: new or wiped gear; a fighter who closes before he reads
batch_2.Q7_waking: A Waking Draft bought on debt: he sells his future to a guild for a Waking Draft (60-120 gold) that often kills or warps; a bought door opens and no more, the fights have to fill it; mid-book turning point
batch_2.Q8_jibe: A hall rule forbids both: the merchant halls bar a sworn fighter from holding a trust title, because a man who is both is buyer and seller of the same blood; 'one has to sell to the other' is the plain-speech gloss of the rule; he means to be the first exception

batch_3.Q9_debt: Lost; her sword turns up: he never learned her name, only her sword's mark; mid-book her blade comes across his counter in a dead man's lot and Provenance lets him read her through it; is she alive, why did she let it go; paying the debt in kind becomes book one's ending
batch_3.Q10_name: Ned Chapman: chapman is the old word for a peddler; people laugh that he was named for his job, and the ones who know the old word laugh harder ('Chapman the chapman')
batch_3.Q11_endgame: Paragon of the halls: the merchant other markets check their own weights against; trusted to sell Unique pieces; for a Paragon the halls come to you
batch_3.Q12_book_one: Stage II, Journeyman: woken by the Draft, two Stages in (Welling), trusted with Uncommon goods; he has taken a fighting hall's yard test and had the hall rule read against him
